# Whether every member of a round-up interval is negative

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `upward_negative_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

A kernel of the round-up interval ([its kernels](upward.md)), of the opt-in header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`). No operation of it rounds: it gives the same result in every rounding mode.

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

Whether $x < 0$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty, $X = [-x_n, x_u]$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies X \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x < 0 \text{ for every } x \in X.$$

A state of the round-up interval is stored as its upper bound and its lower bound negated, the two lanes of one register: $X$ as $(x_u, x_n)$ ([its kernels](upward.md#the-stored-pair)).

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [-x_n, x_u]$, stored as $(x_u, x_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval: the empty set, both lanes a NaN; or a nonempty interval, each lane a number of `T` or $+\infty$ (neither a NaN nor $-\infty$), with $-x_n \le x_u$; its members are the real numbers between $-x_n$ and $x_u$.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $x < 0$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty: the answer is exact.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, no operation of the kernel rounding, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Source

**Algorithm:** the upper bound compared with 0 (the listing of the round-up interval). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/upward_negative_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/upward_negative_1.kernel), the description the formal model (`proofs/gen/UpwardModel.v`) is generated from. The generator prints no C++ of it yet. Each statement is one operation of `T`, and none rounds to nearest ([the round-up interval in the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-round-up-interval)).

```
# Whether every member of an interval of the round-up interval is negative: xu < 0 (xu is never
# -inf, and a NaN makes it false for the empty set); the default interval_negative_1 on the meaning.
# Exact, in every rounding mode (docs/developer/design/upward.md, "Predicates and comparisons").
# Requires the rounding mode upward set by kairn::upward::Scope and the options of
# docs/concepts/upward.md (GCC and Clang -frounding-math, MSVC /fp:strict).

m = lt(xu, 0)
```
